newsitem.title: UK: TABLE TENNIS-CHINA AND SWEDEN MAKE SOLID START.
newsitem.headline: TABLE TENNIS-CHINA AND SWEDEN MAKE SOLID START.

text.p: China and Sweden, the heavyweights of table tennis who have contested six of the last seven men's team finals, received some bruising but no lasting damage on the opening day of the 40th world championships on Thursday.
Both scored 3-1 victories in the first of their five round-robin matches, with defending champions China defeating Slovenia and Sweden emerging on top against Slovakia.

The day's Chinese victim was Ding Song, rated the best defensive player in the world, who fell 21-12 12-21 21-15 against Robert Smrekar. But there was never a hint of a China crisis, even in the absence of Olympic silver medallist Wang Tao who was rested.

In the women's event, China look a certain bet to add to their 10 titles since 1975. They started with a convincing 3-0 win over Russia with Deng Yaping, the only woman to have completed the grand slam, looking in supreme form.
